rv.q: Geoffrey Rush delivers a towering performance as the dying monarch in Ionesco's absurdist masterpiece, making this Broadway revival an essential theatrical experience.
Geoffrey Rush manages a mesmerizing high-wire act of balancing outrageous comedy and overwhelming tragedy in a fascinating revival
"And later, when the king realizes, "One can't live badly - it's a contradiction in terms," the play feels not just absurd, but absurdly wise.'
Regardless, Ionesco's account of a ruler who squanders his time is well worth yours.
The cast is uniformly strong, but this is Rush's show.
His vivid portrayal of human frailties is simply sensational as he takes us on an insightful journey to his ultimate acceptance of his eminent death.
